repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend on main at 59fa027: the Import Notification Service front door, a Hapi and Nunjucks app. Its pages live in src/server/app (about 30,000 lines with unit tests, about 9,000 without). src/server/app/features holds the routed features, listed in features/index.js: dashboard (the INS home at '/', about 260 lines of code and template plus a 137-line fit spec), notification-type (the choose-a-notification-type page and the hand-over into the animals and plants journeys, about 270 lines plus a 179-line fit spec), and address-book (about 4,000 lines of code, templates and copy plus about 4,000 lines of fit specs and fit helpers in address-book/fit): the list with tabs and type filter, add with its address-type step, view, edit and delete for addresses, and transporter type, private and commercial add, view, edit and delete pages, plus the hand-off context, journey registry and return-to logic that let a journey borrow the address book. address-lookup-spike is a dev-and-local-only page routed from app/routes.js. src/server/app/shared holds the layout, error templates, page kit, paths, list-page helper and shared copy (English and Welsh); page-maturity holds the maturity banner; app/auth holds the sign-in templates; lib/validate the form validators; services the address-book, transporters, ins-backend, countries and address-lookup clients and their stubs; docs the repo's own feature and architecture notes. There is no rulings or decisions ledger in the repo (no spec/ or decisions file). Left out of scope: the server plumbing in src/auth, src/plugins, src/config and src/server outside app (sign-in mechanics, CSRF, session cache, logging, health), the client JavaScript and stylesheets, the lighthouse tooling, the unit tests (*.test.js; the fit specs are the scope's tests), src/server/common/test-helpers except the journey hand-shake helper, and the developer process docs docs/testing.md, docs/lighthouse.md and docs/add-a-page.md. The capture fixture services/_capture/fixtures/countries.json is reference data, MDM's content, and is not read. The scope is cut into 8 parts by what a user sees.

Extracted in 8 parts:
Part 1, Shared layout, copy and page kit: Part 1, shared layout, copy and page kit. Read in full: src/server/app/routes.js and features/index.js (route composition); shared/layout.njk (GOV.UK template with header, service navigation, phase banner, maturity banner include, back link, recoverable-error banner, journey strip, two-thirds or full content column, footer); shared/error.njk and error-summary.njk; shared/copy.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js and copy-leaves.js (locale resolution, the shared chrome copy and validator default messages in English and machine-draft Welsh); shared/kit.js (base view model, surfaces, error summary model, draft journey strip, organisation guard, page route builder); shared/paths.js (every INS page path and the two section tests that drive the active navigation item); shared/list-page.js (page parsing, clamping, results label and pagination links); shared/escape-html.js; page-maturity/banner.njk, levels.js, page-maturity.js and its en/cy copy (four maturity levels shown as a second phase banner); app/auth/page.js and the four sign-in templates (unauthorised and the three hidden IDM test pages); src/config/nunjucks/context/context.js (view context: nav urls, active item, user session, crumb, maturity); the fit specs features/page-title.fit.spec.js (9 tests) and fit/smoke.fit.spec.js (1 test) and the fit helpers fit/error-focus.js and fit/axe.js; and the repo's notes docs/README.md (served route list), architecture.md (chassis and application split, error and auth pages, templates, client assets, enforced boundaries, how INS differs from the journey frontends), features.md (feature shapes, paths, page kit, controller shape, copy and templates, validation, client JavaScript, the temporary address-lookup spike, tests) and services.md (barrel/client/stub shape, run mode, each service's contract, configuration, out of scope). Claims cover the chrome every page shares, every shared copy string with its Welsh twin, every path builder, the paging helper, the maturity levels, the sign-in templates, every test in the two specs and the conventions the docs record, as existing rulings. Feature-specific detail the docs repeat for the address book's own pages (fields, roles, tabs, return-to) is left to the parts that own those pages.
Part 2, INS home dashboard: Part 2, the INS home dashboard. Read in full: features/dashboard/page.js (page id and maturity), controller.js (the GET route at '/', query parsing, the calls to countries and ins-backend, the view model and the outage branch), template.njk (heading, Create new button, search form, sort form, empty, no-results, results label, clear search, table and pagination), view-model/list.js (the four sort options, query string building, row mapping, the link rule by status, arrival date formatting), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (every string, English and machine-draft Welsh), fit/dashboard.js (the fit helpers), dashboard.fit.spec.js (8 tests), and services/ins-backend client.js, index.js and stub.js (the GET /notifications request, the organisation guard and the four seeded stub notifications). To check what the code does, I also looked at shared/paths.js, shared/list-page.js, the recoverable-error banner lines of shared/layout.njk and shared/kit.js, lib/validate/calendar.js's display date format, common/helpers/set-base-url.js and services/stub-seed.js. I claim only what those files do on this page. The page has no status tags, no filters other than search and sort, and no summary counts or cards. Those are recorded as gaps where the scope expects them.
Part 3, Notification type and journey hand-shake: Part 3, notification type and journey hand-shake. Read in full: the notification-type feature (page.js, controller.js, destinations.js, template.njk, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, fit/notification-type.js and notification-type.fit.spec.js, with its imported hand-overs.test-support.js), common/constants/journey-set-bases.js, and the address-book hand-shake modules (handshake-context.js, journey-registry.js, return-to.js, success-message.js, record-id-params.js, fit/return-query.js) plus common/test-helpers/journey-handshake.js. Also read, for context only, common/helpers/set-base-url.js (how a set base URL is joined), shared/paths.js (the notification-type path and the dashboard section) and a few lines of address-book/add/add.controller.js where the hand-shake's cancel and landing values are used. Covered: the /notification-type page (route, maturity, heading, caption, four radio options and their order, the validation error, the Continue button, the back link, the hand-over to the animals and plants start entries, and the returning-notification path back to a live animals notification's origin page), the three journey set bases and the frontend each points at, the hand-shake context (the four query or payload fields, refusal when incomplete or unlisted, session storage), the journey registry (two journey types, five party fulfilment ids and the role each maps to, the return URL shape and its landing values), the return query rules (which returns are honoured and which refused), the success message carried in the session, the record id validation, and all nine tests of the notification-type fit spec. The address book pages themselves are other parts.
Part 4, Address book list: Part 4, Address book list. Read in full: features/address-book/list/page.js (1 line, maturity), list.controller.js (395 lines: the GET handler, tab and type-filter selection, page loading and clamping, table heads and rows for addresses and transporters, the failed-load view), list.njk (101 lines: success banner, h1, intro, Add a new address button, the Filter addresses details holding the search box, search button and Type select, the MOJ sub-navigation tabs, panel h2, results line, Clear search link, table and pagination), view-model/list.js (134 lines: query strings, name lines, results label, role and transporter-type label search, row mapping for both tables), address-book-tabs.js (43 lines: three tabs and their type filters), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (only the list keys and notApplicable are claimed here; the rest belongs to other parts), services/address-book client.js, index.js, stub.js, address-types.js, typed-seed.js and services/address-book-request.js (what the list sends to and gets from the address-book API, the stub's seeds and matching), and the fit helpers address-book-list.js, address-book-list-text.js, seed-address.js and every test in list.fit.spec.js (45 tests in 13 describe blocks, counting each parameterised case once per loop). To read cells and paging exactly, shared/list-page.js, shared/paths.js, address-book/fields.js and address-book/address-countries.js were also read, and are cited only where a list claim rests on them. Covered: the list route and heading, intro, add button, success banner slot, filter disclosure, search box with label and hint, Type filter and its options per tab, Clear search, the three tabs and their headings, both tables' columns and how each cell reads, results line and empty state, page size, pagination and page clamping, the load-failure behaviour, the address types and roles and how they group, the list request the client sends, the stub's list behaviour and seeds, the Welsh twins of the list keys, and every fit test. Not covered here: the add, view, edit and delete pages and the transporter tab's own pages, and the shared recoverable-error copy (shared layout part).
Part 5, Add an address: Part 5, Add an address. Read in full: the address-type step (address-type/page.js, address-type.controller.js, address-type.njk), the add page (add/page.js, add.controller.js, add.njk), the shared address-fields.njk macro, fields.js (field rules), field-rule.js, address-countries.js, add-in-progress.js (the session store for an add in progress), stored-address.js, lines-html.js, the address-book copy in English and Welsh (copy.en.js, copy.cy.js; only the add, addressType, form, roles, add success banner and field error keys claimed here), lib/validate (index.js, run.js, validators.js, calendar.js), the countries service (client.js, index.js, stub.js), and the fit helper address-form.js with the two fit specs add.fit.spec.js and address-type.fit.spec.js. Also looked up, for routes and roles only: shared/paths.js (address-book, add and address-type paths and the start query) and services/address-book/address-types.js (address types, form types, roles by type, place roles), and the ROLES_BY_PARTY table in common/test-helpers/journey-handshake.js. Covered: two pages. The address-type page at /address-book/add/address-type (three radio options with hints, one error, Continue, Back, where each option leads, the start query that clears an add in progress). The add page at /address-book/add in its two modes: the address-book mode (after the address-type step, roles question by address type, Save and continue, Cancel and return to address book, success banner and landing on the type's list tab) and the role-handshake mode a notification journey opens (journey strip, the other-roles question, Save and select, Save and return to address page, Cancel and return to hub). For both: every address and contact field with label, hint, width, autocomplete, required and maximum length, the country select and how its list is built from reference data, every validation message in English and Welsh, error handling when the address book refuses or fails, and what is saved. Every validator exported by lib/validate with its limits, and which ones the address fields use. Every test in the two fit specs, a looped test claimed once naming its instances. The handshake context, return URL and journey registry mechanics themselves are part 3's; the list the add lands on is part 4's; view, edit and delete are part 6's.
Part 6, View, edit and delete an address: Part 6, View, edit and delete an address. Read in full: the view, edit and delete feature folders under src/server/app/features/address-book (page.js, controller, njk for each), the shared address-fields.njk macro, copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (claiming only the view, edit, delete, success-banner, notApplicable and form keys these pages render), and the fit specs view.fit.spec.js (17 tests incl. 3 generated ignored-return tests), edit.fit.spec.js (18 tests) and delete.fit.spec.js (14 tests). Supporting files consulted for accuracy only, not claimed in full: shared/paths.js (routes), return-to.js (return and leave destinations) and fields.js (field list and display text). Covered: three pages. View at /address-book/{id}: heading is the address name, a summary list of the address and contact fields, Edit and Delete buttons, Back link, dead-link redirects. Edit at /address-book/{id}/edit: prefilled address-fields form under Address and Contact details, Save changes and Cancel, validation re-render, save to the address book keeping roles, success banner on the list. Delete at /address-book/{id}/delete: one-row Address summary, confirmation and warning paragraphs, Yes, delete and No, cancel, success banner only when landing on the list, stale and dead-link handling. Field validation rules themselves are part 5's.
Part 7, Transporters: Part 7, Transporters. Read in full: the 18 files under src/server/app/features/address-book/transporter/ (page.js; the transporter type, private add and commercial add controllers and views; the shared transporter-fields.njk macros; transporter-summary.js and transporter-return.js; the view, edit (edit.controller.js, edit-form.js, edit-private.njk, edit-commercial.njk) and delete controllers and views), the address-book helpers transporter-fields.js, transporter-navigation.js, transporter-save.js, transporter-in-progress.js and stored-transporter.js, the address-book copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (only transporter keys claimed: transporterType, privateTransporterForm, commercialTransporterForm, editTransporter, deleteTransporter, the transporter success banners, the transporter errors, plus list.transporterTypes, list.table.approvalNumber/type and view.edit/delete as the view page uses them), the transporters service (client.js, index.js, stub.js, transporter-types.js), the fit helper transporter-form.js and the 5 transporter fit specs (type 6 tests, forms 11 tests, view 4, edit 4, delete 3). Route paths were confirmed from shared/paths.js lines 3-28. Covered: the 7 transporter pages (type question at /address-book/add/transporter, private add at /private, commercial add at /commercial, view at /address-book/transporter/{id}, edit at /edit with a private and a commercial form, delete at /delete), their copy, fields, validation, navigation, session state and saving; the PRIVATE and COMMERCIAL types and the Northern Ireland country rule; the address-book transporters API client and in-memory stub; the Welsh twins; and every fit test. The list's Transporter tab itself is part 4's.
Part 8, Address lookup spike: Part 8, Address lookup spike. Read in full: src/server/app/routes.js (the spike's conditional registration only), src/server/app/features/address-lookup-spike/ page.js, is-dev-or-local.js, controller.js, template.njk, detect-search-mode.js, map-to-address-fields.js, copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js, plus src/server/app/services/address-lookup/ client.js, index.js and stub.js, and kit.pageRoutes for the route shape. The slice is one page at /address-lookup-spike, registered only in the dev and local environments. It has a single form (search term), a postcode-or-free-text mode detection, a results list where each result has a 'Use this address' button, a backend timings table, a mapped-address summary list with the fields the lookup could not fill, and a raw-JSON details block. The service layer calls the INS backend's /address-lookup endpoint, or an in-memory stub of three fixed addresses in stub mode. The page has no links and saves nothing. Claims cover the route and its gate, every branch of the POST handler, the mode detection, the field mapping and its gap messages, every English copy string and its Welsh twin, the client request and the stub response.
